title: A sudo relay request gets back only its own result, under its own timeout
intention: A root request through the sudo relay gets back only its own result, under its own timeout, and a result nobody collected is a loud finding rather than the next request's answer.
why: Two defects reproduced in a scratch relay dir: await_result returns whatever relay/done holds, so a leftover result is handed to the next request as its own (a command that never ran read rc 0), and process_pending ignores the client's timeout (executor runs under its 120s default). Akien asked for the fix and will restart the daemon (/home/akien/.cairn/foreground-decisions.md line 437) and cleared teeth (1)-(4) ('yes to all four, go', line 471).
traces_to: Law 7 (a record of truth never collapses an error): today a stale done is returned as the next request's result, so a command that never ran reports rc 0 (measured: B's await returned 'echo A-yesterday rc 0' while B's pending.sh sat unrun); and the telos aim of getting Akien out of running the system, which needs CC's root path to tell the truth.
how: In cairn/devices/sudo_relay/relay.py: request_root mints a request id at submit; the request is written as relay/pending.json {id, command, timeout_s} (a new filename, so the old daemon running until Akien's restart never runs a JSON payload as bash); process_pending runs the executor with timeout=timeout_s and writes relay/done/<id>.json and the audit record under that same id; await_result(id) reads only its own file; a done/<id>.json no live request awaits is an orphan, never returned, listed in SudoRelayDevice.state() as orphaned_results and named by a breadcrumb on the request that finds it. Four new teeth in cairn/devices/sudo_relay/proofs/test_sudo_relay.py. Questions a Haiku-level builder would need, answered here, all in cairn/devices/sudo_relay/relay.py: Names? Replace _PENDING='pending.sh', _EXECUTING='executing.sh', _DONE='done' (relay.py:87-89) with _PENDING='pending.json', _EXECUTING='executing.json', _RESULTS='results', _AWAITING='awaiting', and keep _LEGACY_DONE='done' only so orphaned_results() can read a file the old daemon left. Id? audit_record (relay.py:128) gains a keyword rid: str | None = None and uses it as 'id' when given. submit(command, *, timeout_s: float = 120.0) -> str (relay.py:211): rid = _mint_id(datetime.now(timezone.utc)); touch awaiting/<rid>; write pending.json {id, command, timeout_s} via a temp file + os.replace; return rid. process_pending (relay.py:220): read pending.json -> os.replace to executing.json -> json.load; executor(command, timeout=timeout_s); record = audit_record(..., rid=req['id']); write_audit as today; write results/<rid>.json via temp + os.replace; unlink executing.json. await_result(rid, *, timeout, poll) (relay.py:248): poll results/<rid>.json ONLY; on hit load, unlink it and awaiting/<rid>, return; on deadline unlink awaiting/<rid> and raise TimeoutError naming rid. request_root(command, *, timeout) (relay.py:268): rid = submit(command, timeout_s=timeout); return await_result(rid, timeout=timeout + _AWAIT_GRACE_S) with _AWAIT_GRACE_S = 5.0, so a command the daemon times out still comes home as its record. New orphaned_results() -> list[str]: ids of results/*.json with no awaiting/<id> marker, plus the id inside a legacy relay/done file if one exists; never deletes. SudoRelayDevice.request_root (relay.py:391): after the existing 'request_root' emit, if orphaned_results() is non-empty emit 'orphaned_results' with pointer=the first id and values={'orphans': [ids]}. SudoRelayDevice.state() (relay.py:415) adds 'orphaned_results': orphaned_results(). Proof: in test_protocol_runs_the_command_and_returns_the_truth, rid = relay.submit(...) and relay.await_result(rid, timeout=2.0), same assertions; add the four teeth, a PROVES block mapping '1'-'4' to them under this ticket's id, and add them to _main's checks. daemon.py is unchanged: it calls process_pending(relay.root_executor, now=now).
falsifier: Falsifier: cairn/devices/sudo_relay/proofs/test_sudo_relay.py green under bin/cairn test at HEAD with its nine existing teeth and four new ones: (1) test_a_leftover_result_is_never_returned — a legacy relay/done and a results/<old-id>.json from earlier requests stand on disk; request_root('echo mine', timeout=10) against a one-iteration daemon thread returns the record whose command is 'echo mine' and whose id is the id this request minted, and both leftovers are still on disk; (2) test_an_unanswered_request_times_out_rather_than_taking_anothers — the same leftovers, no daemon: request_root('echo nobody-runs-this', timeout=0.5) raises TimeoutError naming its own id, and both leftovers are still on disk; (3) test_the_daemon_runs_under_the_requests_timeout — a recording executor handed a request submitted with timeout_s=7 is called with timeout=7; through the device, 'sleep 3' under timeout=1 returns returncode None with '[sudo_relay] timed out after 1s' in stderr, and 'sleep 0.2' under timeout=10 returns returncode 0; (4) test_an_orphan_is_a_loud_finding — with the two leftovers on disk, SudoRelayDevice.state()['orphaned_results'] lists both ids, and a request_root round-trip holds exactly two breadcrumbs, 'request_root' then 'orphaned_results' whose values name both ids. Every one of (1)-(4) reds with relay.py reverted to its pre-build commit. Horizon: this voyage; the first live reading is Akien's daemon restart after PROVED.

decisions.text: relay.py only. Constants _PENDING='pending.json', _EXECUTING='executing.json', _RESULTS='results', _AWAITING='awaiting', _LEGACY_DONE='done', _AWAIT_GRACE_S=5.0. audit_record(..., rid=None) uses rid as the id when given. submit(command, *, timeout_s=120.0) -> str mints rid with _mint_id(datetime.now(timezone.utc)), touches awaiting/<rid>, writes pending.json {id, command, timeout_s} by temp file + os.replace, returns rid. process_pending os.replace's pending.json to executing.json, json.loads it, builds the record with audit_record(rid=req id), write_audit, writes results/<rid>.json by temp + replace, unlinks executing.json. await_result(rid, *, timeout, poll) polls ONLY results/<rid>.json; on a hit loads it, unlinks it and the awaiting marker, returns the record; at the deadline unlinks the marker and raises TimeoutError naming rid. request_root(command, *, timeout): rid = submit(command, timeout_s=timeout); return await_result(rid, timeout=timeout + _AWAIT_GRACE_S). daemon.py unchanged.
decisions.step: unlisted: mint the request id in relay.py

decisions.text: In process_pending the executor call becomes executor(command, timeout=timeout_s) with timeout_s read from the pending payload; local_executor/root_executor already take timeout= and _run already returns (None, out, err + '[sudo_relay] timed out after Ns') on expiry. No executor signature changes.
decisions.step: unlisted: pass the request's timeout to the executor

decisions.text: New module function orphaned_results() -> list[str]: the ids of results/*.json with no awaiting/<id> marker, plus the id inside a legacy relay/done when one exists; it never deletes. SudoRelayDevice.request_root, after its existing 'request_root' emit, emits 'orphaned_results' with pointer = the first id and values = {'orphans': ids} when the list is non-empty. state() gains the key 'orphaned_results'. The audit record's six fields are unchanged.
decisions.step: unlisted: orphaned_results read loudly, nothing deleted

decisions.text: The legacy relay/done is a single FILE at <instance>/relay/done, written by today's process_pending as json.dumps(record) of the six-field audit record; its id is the record's 'id' key (the proof's _plant_leftovers writes exactly that). orphaned_results() reads it with json.loads(text)['id']; if the file cannot be parsed or has no 'id', the literal name 'done' is listed instead, so the leftover is still named. The file is never written, consumed or deleted by the new code.
